solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pipe down building placed in position

indicators.note: the building is set down inside the word for position, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to sit is to be in position, as a model sits for a portrait
a hut is a simple building

explanation.surface: A building is lowered into its intended spot on site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe down' looks like plumbing beside 'building', but it is the slang order to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are blunt commands telling someone to stop talking, an informal idiom for silence.

clue.text: Associate with tramp holding new book

indicators.note: the tramp contains the letter for new

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp

explanation.surface: Someone keeps company with a vagrant clutching a fresh book.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix socially or rub shoulders, especially with people of higher status.

clue.text: Farewell horrendous lepidoptera — none seen for ages?

indicators.note: the letters are made a horrible mess and rearranged
the nought appears in place of the ages, replacing them

parts.note: an era is an age, a long period
O is zero, none

explanation.surface: Goodbye to horrible butterflies and moths, none spotted in years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen for' swaps ERA in lepidoptera for O, leaving LEPIDOPTO, which 'horrendous' rearranges. The answer is old-fashioned British slang for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunty, dated British way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Having strayed, turn to her for direction

indicators.note: letters that have wandered off course end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A lost traveller turns to a woman for guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: The geographic pole bearing is a compass direction, distinct from magnetic north.

clue.text: Report of girl deceived by a snake

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so what follows is said aloud and the sound gives the letters

parts.note: a girl, Anna, conned by an 'a' is spoken as Anna conned a

explanation.surface: A news story about a young woman tricked by somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'Anna conned a' quickly and it sounds like the big South American snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge constricting serpent of South American rivers, one particular kind of snake.

clue.text: Dreaded meow as feline finally moves

indicators.note: the letters move around into a new order
take the closing letter of feline

explanation.surface: A cat's terrifying meow as it finally stirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges MEOW AS into AWESOM; the last letter of feline adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: In its old sense the word means inspiring awe or dread, so something feared.

clue.text: Silver inscribed with second name between

indicators.note: the silver has the other letters written into it

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A silver item engraved with a second name in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both prepositions mean in the midst of or surrounded by.

clue.text: One between legs — potential cause of tears?

indicators.note: the one goes in the middle of the pair

parts.note: leg side in cricket is the on side, so legs gives two ONs
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone between the legs, possibly causing tears.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so two legs are ON ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping this vegetable makes the eyes water, so it may bring tears.

clue.text: Groom on time as horse moves

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to dress is to groom, as with hair or a horse
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A stable hand works on time while the horse moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Equestrian discipline in which a horse performs precise trained steps and manoeuvres.

clue.text: Rank ratings given by old music-maker

parts.note: ABS are able seamen, ratings in the navy
a lute is a stringed instrument that makes music

explanation.surface: Sailors are ranked in some order by an elderly musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' reads as a verb but is the adjective meaning utter, as in a rank beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives both mean complete or utter, as in a rank amateur or an utter fool.

clue.text: Duck pâté ingredient for celebrity chef

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, the shape O
liver is the classic base of pâté

explanation.surface: Duck liver pâté as a dish served by a famous cook.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamie Oliver is a well-known British television cook, so the surname names a celebrity chef.

clue.text: Drop round to grab length in material

indicators.note: the phrase for a visit seizes the length letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to drop round is to pop in, pay a casual visit

explanation.surface: Someone drops in to fetch a length of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop round' reads as something falling in a circle, but it is a casual visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplin is a plain-woven cotton fabric used for shirts, a kind of material.

clue.text: One pulls out the stops roasting nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of roasting go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone goes all-out while roasting a batch of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulls out the stops' sounds like trying hard, but literally means drawing an organ's stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A church musician at the keyboard literally draws the stops to choose the pipes that sound.

clue.text: Timber lifting in Noah's Ark

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting carries the letters upward, reading them backwards
the letters are sitting inside the words

explanation.surface: Wood being raised aboard Noah's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes HSA from Noah's Ark; 'lifting' turns it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardwood tree whose wood is used for tool handles, a type of timber.

clue.text: Deal involving organ transplant?

parts.note: a transplant swaps one body part for another, so it is literally a trade of parts

explanation.surface: A grim bargain over surgery to swap a body organ.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a part exchange is a sale where an old item, typically a car, is handed in towards the price of a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in purchase where the old item counts towards the new is literally a swap of parts.

clue.text: Sound cut in shout to encourage knight

indicators.note: the shortened sound word goes inside the shout

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of encouragement

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: sound as in a sound argument means valid

explanation.surface: A cut sound within a rousing shout to spur on a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is valid, as a sound argument, not a noise; 'cut' leaves VALI.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a horseman is used for a knight or member of an order of chivalry.

clue.text: Write number appearing within a small range

indicators.note: the writing and the number show up inside the outer letters

parts.note: to pen is to write
nine is a number

explanation.surface: Write down a figure that falls inside a narrow span.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a set of values but is mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain chain running down the length of Italy is a range.

clue.text: Aussie opening pair, having turned, run one extra bye

indicators.note: the first two letters of Aussie
the following pieces are turned back to front

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
I is the Roman numeral one
over means extra, as in left over

explanation.surface: Australian openers in cricket score a run and a bye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having turned' reverses R I OVER to give REVOIR. Bye and extra are both cricket words on the surface; here bye is short for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is a parting salutation, the same as a casual farewell.

clue.text: Dishonestly take position as head waiter?

definitions.text: Dishonestly take position as head waiter?

parts.words: Dishonestly take position as head waiter?
parts.note: a waiter here is someone waiting in line; pushing to the front unfairly makes you head of the line

explanation.surface: A restaurant employee cheats their way to the top job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head waiter' suggests a restaurant boss, but means the first of those waiting in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing in ahead of people already waiting in line is unfairly taking the front spot.

clue.text: Call for Terence

definitions.meaning: .... is the short form for a telephone number, one to call
a pet form of the name Terence, popular in London

explanation.surface: Someone is told to ring a man called Terence.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for telephone, and also the usual familiar form of Terence, as with footballer Terry Venables.

clue.text: This could contribute to change in US district

definitions.text: This could contribute to change in US
definitions.meaning: a twenty-five cent coin makes up part of the loose change in an American pocket
an area of a city, as in the Latin part of Paris

explanation.surface: A small part of change in an American neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A US coin worth a fourth of a dollar, and also a section of a town.

clue.text: Simple farmer one used to steer

definitions.meaning: a person who tills the soil, a farmer in its simplest description
a lever that turns a boat's rudder

explanation.surface: An unsophisticated farmer is the one who steers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ploughs land, and also the bar attached to a boat's rudder for steering.

clue.text: Dish with wheat base is no meal for cooking

indicators.note: the words are put in the pot and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A wheat-based dish is declared not a proper meal once cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is coarse durum wheat flour, cooked as a milk pudding, so a wheat-based dish.

clue.text: Perhaps return to university and study Nash?

indicators.note: the going is turned back, reading the letters in reverse

parts.note: you go to university, so the phrase stands for go
a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: A student goes back to college to read the poet Nash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nash' looks like the subject of study, but it is the definition; 'Perhaps' signals that going to university is only one example of go.
explanation.definitionFit: The American comic poet Ogden Nash is known by both names; this is his first name.

clue.text: One must extinguish second fire in room

indicators.note: the second letter is put out, removed from the word

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: Someone must put out a second blaze in a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extinguish' sounds like firefighting but signals removing the S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a domestic hearth fire, as in inglenook, the fireside corner.

clue.text: Work that caddie, nearby wheeling bags

indicators.note: wheeling turns round, so the caught letters are read backwards
the words bag, or hold, the run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A golf caddie near the green wheels a trolley of bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' takes DIENEA from caddie nearby; 'wheeling' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's Latin epic of Aeneas is a celebrated literary work.

clue.text: Champion boxer possibly?

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of hound, so a winning one might be the best canine in the show

explanation.surface: A boxing title-holder, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' means a fighter on the surface, but the dog breed in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the leader or winner, and a champion boxer dog would literally be the best hound.

clue.text: Muddle keeps right one in complex romantic situation

indicators.note: the muddle holds the other letters, keeping them inside

parts.note: a tangle is a muddle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A confused affair keeps one lover in the right place.
explanation.definitionFit: A love triangle is three people romantically entangled, a messy relationship.

clue.text: Good coin and currency reduced in splendour

parts.note: the rand is the South African unit of money

indicators.note: the currency word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the euro is the currency of much of Europe

explanation.surface: A fine coin and cash, though devalued, shown amid luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificence or splendour of scale and appearance is what the word denotes.

clue.text: Certain prayers are unfinished in optimistic environment

indicators.note: the optimistic word forms the surroundings, enclosing the shortened word

parts.note: rosy means hopeful, as in a rosy outlook

indicators.note: the word are loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Prayers left incomplete amid a hopeful mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic sequence of Hail Marys and other prayers counted on beads, a set of particular prayers.
